facts.text: Eros Ponded Regolith Feature was deployed at Asteroid 433 Eros (South Pole) during NEAR Shoemaker at Eros in 2001.
facts.source: Icarus (Robinson et al. 2002) / NEAR MSI Camera

facts.text: A flat, crater-free 'pond' of ultra-fine dust accumulated in low gravitational depressions on Eros, created by electrostatic levitation and acoustic seismic shaking.
facts.source: Icarus (Robinson et al. 2002) / NEAR MSI Camera

facts.text: Engineered specifically to operate in the harsh vacuum and extreme temperatures of the lunar environment.
Discovered that micrometeorite impacts trigger global seismic vibrations that cause fine electrostatic dust to flow like fluid and settle into completely flat dust ponds.
Status: Remains preserved in the arid regolith at Asteroid 433 Eros (South Pole).
A permanent human and robotic monument celebrating space exploration on the Moon.

scenes.kids: I am Eros Ponded Regolith Feature. I arrived here at Asteroid 433 Eros (South Pole) in 2001.
scenes.explorer: Eros Ponded Regolith Feature, NEAR Shoemaker at Eros: deployed at Asteroid 433 Eros (South Pole) in 2001.

scenes.kids: Take a look at how I was built. Every part of me had a special purpose.
scenes.explorer: A flat, crater-free 'pond' of ultra-fine dust accumulated in low gravitational depressions on Eros, created by electrostatic levitation and acoustic seismic shaking.

scenes.kids: Out here, there is no air or weather like on Earth, so I had to work smoothly in the cold.
scenes.explorer: Designed to withstand radiation, cosmic dust, and extreme temperature swings without failing.

scenes.kids: Discovered that micrometeorite impacts trigger global seismic vibrations that cause fine electrostatic dust to flow like fluid and settle into completely flat dust ponds.
scenes.explorer: Discovered that micrometeorite impacts trigger global seismic vibrations that cause fine electrostatic dust to flow like fluid and settle into completely flat dust ponds.

scenes.kids: My mission finished, but I stay here resting peacefully on the surface.
scenes.explorer: Fate: left on surface. Position recorded at coordinates [-0.5, -5.8].

scenes.kids: Everything I learned showed humanity how to explore deeper into space.
scenes.explorer: A milestone in planetary science and permanent historical artifact.
